study type: case study (with comparison to published controls)
outcome: single-cell transcriptomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)
properties of immune cell subsets (T cells, B cells, NK cells, myeloid cells, CD16 monocytes, MAIT cells)
cohort: The study involved a single pregnant woman who had recovered from COVID-19, with immune cell profiles compared to healthy pregnant controls from published data.
finding: The pregnant woman recovering from COVID-19 showed distinct immune cell profiles with increased myeloid and B cells, decreased T and NK cells, and specific changes in CD16 monocytes (increased proportion, enriched gene sets related to antigen processing/presentation, T-cell activation) and MAIT cells (decreased frequency, enriched gene sets related to antigen processing/presentation, response to type II interferon/virus).
cross-section timing: at 28 weeks of gestation, before a cesarean section
